the short range interactions in graphene can lead to staggered polarization of Dirac sea at $\nu=\mp 1$.
the short ranged SU(2) and SU(4) interactions can induce staggered polarization of a Dirac sea of filled Landau levels.

the symmetry breaking of the quantum Hall states of Dirac fermions.
the symmetry breaking in quantum Hall states of Dirac electrons in graphene.
the study of the quantum Hall effect (QHE) in graphene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed $\nu=1$ state is an AFM state of the sea of Landau-levels.
the observed $\pi$ phase shift is a consequence of the staggered polarization of Dirac-Lane levels in graphene.
the quantum Hall states of the graphene are characterized by a filled Dirac-Landua sea with an anti-ferromagnetically ordered ground state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sea of Diracs can be polarized by the short ranged interactions.
the valley symmetry breaking in graphene is possible in the presence of short ranged SU(2) symmetry breaking interactions.
the valley symmetry breaking in the sea of Dirca-Landau levels can be induced by the short-ranged interactions and this effect can lead to the observed anti-ferromagnetism in graphene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the valley symmetry broken, spin ordered phase is the ground state at $\nu=\frac{1}{4},\frac{3}{4},-\frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{3}{2}$.
the sea of Diral-Landau levels can be polarized in the same way as the valence Landau levels.
